verdict_reason: Present PE (17.52) sits below both Shiller PE (28.01) and the 12yr historical median (19.82) — cheap on a cyclically-adjusted and own-history basis. Not a denominator trick: FY082-083 EPS (23.83) is the second-highest in the 12yr record, so the low PE reflects genuinely strong current earnings, not an EPS spike distorting the ratio.
devils_advocate: A near-peak EPS year is exactly when trailing PE looks most flattering — if 082-083's earnings are a cyclical high (rate-spread tailwind, provisioning reversal) rather than a new run-rate, the 'cheap' read inverts once earnings mean-revert toward the 12yr average (~15.4 vs this year's 23.83). Technicals aren't confirming a re-rating either: price is pinned near its own 60-day resistance (Rs.427) with RSI14 at 64 (approaching overbought), and the stock is down -14.47% over 1yr. NPL%/revenue detail isn't available from local/auto-scraped data, so the earnings-quality question behind this print (core margin expansion vs one-off) can't be confirmed without the annual report or a ShareSansar Pro deep dive.
